summary:
# NOTES: 'GAINST THE MIGHT OF SPAIN (Percy F. Westerman; Gutenberg #78984; Pilgrim Press, London; illus. Savile Lumley)
Single book. Narrator Ralph Roy, first person. Ch. I-XXV.

## Characters
- **Ralph Roy** (narrator): b. 6 July 1568, Crofton, Hampshire. Age 12 at father's disappearance; 14 when bound 'prentice; 16 on 1584 voyage (birthday, day after Lady Day). Knighted as Sir Ralph Roy by Queen Elizabeth (ch. XXV).
- **Richard Roy** (father): Queen's pilot, Titchfield Haven; b. ~1541; once brought Philip of Spain's ship to Southampton. Scars on back. Ex-Spanish Main venture; ~1566 returned. Abducted by Spanish from Titchfield (fake pinnace *Speedie* of Brixham, galeas of Cadiz); held at Escorial, tortured; Don Iago claimed him. Later prisoner in Inquisition castle. Escaped with Ralph; lost left foot at ankle in fight with *Sol del Esto* (ch. XIX); at Crofton/Portsmouth thereafter.
- **Mother** (Mistress Roy): unnamed; sold home, moved to Portsmouth.
- **Jack Staynton**: son of Roger; 2 years older than Ralph, 3 inches shorter, broad; hot-headed, good-hearted. Stowaway in hold of *Damsel of Lyme* (ch. IV-V), put ashore at Portsmouth by fishing shallop; later rejoins on *Nonsuch*; later sails to Pacific.
- **Roger Staynton**: master-gunner of Portsmouth. Past: refused burgess-ship; hauled gun to Mayor's house, chained Mayor astride it; fled to Flanders, served Dutch. Returned Elizabeth's reign. Friend of Hannibal Cleat. Later sells office, fits out *Nonsuch*; becomes Captain Staynton. Silver whistle on neck.
- **Hannibal Cleat** (Captain): tall, bearded, cropped head, straight brows, blue serge jerkin, silver whistle on chain, sheath-knife, wallet. Bought *Damsel of Lyme* for £34 at sale. Pirate; cruel; shouts constantly; oaths. Whipped Ralph at mast (ch. V). Mortally wounded in fight with Spanish caravel (ch. VII); went mad, ordered Ralph to fire powder under cabin (Jack hidden there); pistol misfire; died of collapse (ch. VIII). Body weighted and thrown overboard.
- **James** (seaman, "first mate"): red-faced, curly-headed, vile temper; sided with Cleat.
- **Old Garge** (seaman): ~40, tall, sparse; kindly; washed Ralph's wounds; saved Dick Buzza.
- **Dick Buzza**: Cornish boy, <10, of sloop *Jane* of Padstow (bound Ipswich); vanished at Ralph's search (ch. VIII).
- **Don Iago d'Alvarez**: Spanish grandee, ~50, tall, slender, bronze, narrow beady eyes, pointed black beard, jewelled fingers. Partner of Richard Roy; betrayed him at Rio del Foy. Captain of *San Josef*. Lived in villa, Spanish port (Vigo implied). Demanded silver-mine chart. Later captured for piracy, condemned to galleys (ch. XXV).
- **José da Silva**: Don, co-conspirator; captain of *Sol del Esto*; killed at its capture.
- **Coombes** (John Coombes, mate, Bosham): led swim to recover *Damsel* at Rio estuary; later took command in fireship action.
- **Skelton**: seaman; spiked gun; hurled hammer; broke rib.
- **Jenkins**: seaman; kicked off ledge by mule; rescued by rope and dagger.
- **Cox**: skilled leech (surgeon) on *Damsel*.
- **Tom Slingsby** (Sir Thomas Slingsby, of Bramdean nr Winchester): joined at Portsmouth with 4 musketeers (paid £100 offer; refused payment). Wounded in *Venetian* action (shoulder), then stabbed by boarder; recovers.
- **Master Welsh**: injured; replaced on fireship mission.
- **Captain Young, Captain Prowse**: fireship commanders; Prowse in *Daisy*.
- **Master Matthews**: provisions merchant (Portsmouth).
- **Smith**: Portsmouth miller.
- **Master Long**: owner-captain *Minx* (Portsmouth).
- **Thomas Fleming**: Scottish pirate, Leith; pardoned by Howard after bringing news.
- **Master Green**: Admiral's chirurgeon.
- **Sir Henry Radclyffe**: Governor of Portsmouth; later Earl of Sussex; vouched for Ralph.
- **John Highfield**: Mayor (1582); **Owen Tottye**: former mayor, magistrate; bound Ralph (indenture, 6 years, £5 premium); **Master Ridge**: apothecary, told Jack's parents; **Master Jennyns**: neighbour cloth-merchant; **Master William Terge** (*Loyalty*), **Dionysius Savage** (*Ark*): masters Ralph might have bound to; **Giles Bickley**: host of the Star inn.
- Ship names: *Speedie* (Brixham pinnace, decoy); *Damsel of Lyme* (pinnace, 21 tuns, ~50 ft, ex-pirate, later rigged as felucca); *Nonsuch* (barque of Dartmouth, 200 tons, Staynton's); *Venture* (lost off Texel); *Golden Cross* (Queen's ship, Capt. Amyas Thorrogood); *Jane* (sloop, Padstow); *San Josef* (galleon, Don Iago's); *Sol del Esto* (galleon, da Silva's; formerly "*Sol del Esto*" captured); *Distaff* (armed merchantman); *Pride of Saltash* (pinnace; topmast lent by old owner); *Defiance*, *Alarm*, *Revenge* (Drake's), *Ark Royal* (Howard's flagship), *Triumph*, *Raven*, *Speedwell*, *Daisy*, *Pearl*, *Enterprise*, *Minx*, *Nonpareil*, *St. Matthew*; Venetian ship at Goodwins.

## Places
Crofton (Hampshire, home; Place House, Lord Wriothesley's mansion at Titchfield); Titchfield Haven; Southampton; Portsmouth (Camber, Point, Quay Gate, Star inn, Three Crowns, Blue Anchor, Guildhall, St Thomas's bell, Hog Market Street, Dragon/Lyon/White Hart/Rose inns); Calshot Castle; Hurst Castle; Lymington; Solent; Isle of Wight; Land's End; Brittany (Plougastel); Corunna/Finisterre; Vigo (Spanish port, Inquisition prison, St Thomé priory chapel); Vera Cruz; Rio del Foy; mine of San Luis (Mexico); volcano Huitzel; Yucatan; bay of Campechy; Virginia colony; Bahamas; Lizard; Fowey; Plymouth Sound/Catwater/Mount's Bay; Rame Head; Looe; Penlee; Ushant; Scilly; Calais Roads; Goodwins; Tilbury; Whitehall; Firth of Forth; Bordeaux.

## Events in order
1. 1568 Ralph born. 1554 Philip's ship brought by Richard Roy. ~1560s Mexico adventure; mules driven over ravine; back 1566; married.
2. Night of ~twelfth year: flat calm; midnight hail "Speedie of Brixham"; Richard goes with stranger; never returns. Storm next day; Mother: "did he talk like an Englishman?" Devon man.
3. Ralph ~14, Portsmouth. Jack and Ralph see *Damsel of Lyme* arrested by Vice-Admiral Horsey; sale set 29 June 1582. Roger intervenes with Governor vs Mayor. Ralph & Jack board pinnace. Cleat appears; Roger reunites with him.
4. Cleat buys pinnace (£34); takes Ralph (indenture £5, six years). Jack stows in cabin trapdoor/hold. Discovered; put off on shallop. Cleat whips Ralph at mast. Crew: ex-prisoners freed from *Nonsuch* (were to hang).
5. Piracy: Hollander (refused); sloop *Jane* sunk on reef by Runnelstone; boy Dick Buzza spared by Garge; Brittany port sale.
6. Plougastel → Corunna convoy. Caravel (Hispaniola fleet) attacked; Cleat boards, wounded. Dick Buzza vanishes. Cleat's madness; pistol misfire; dies. Ralph alone; mast lost in squall; Spanish galleon *San Josef* boards; Ralph taken.
7. *San Josef*: Don Iago proposes deal (chart of mine in Crofton house). Ralph refuses; bilboes; storm; leak; ship anchors at Vigo. Ralph in villa; sees father's Southampton chart. Imprisoned in Inquisition castle, cell 19. Found father in neighboring cell; father told history (Escorial; King Philip; galeas trap).
8. Inquisition trial: Ralph sentenced to burning (sacrilege; stolen crucifix from Cartagena cathedral). Father and Ralph overpower four familiars, Inquisitors slain. Escape in familiars' garb through secret passage to St Thomé chapel, over wall, boat to fishing port; recover *Damsel* (rigged as felucca), escape under cannon fire.
9. *Damsel* adrift; galley attack; father's leg; *Nonsuch* (Capt. Staynton, Roger) rescues; Jack aboard. Fowey; winter; Roger's partnership; Queen's permission (1584). Plan from Crofton house.
10. Mexico: 31 June? (last day June) 1584 landing, 70 men; Indians; burning mountain Huitzel; pass with rope rescue of Jenkins; mine reached (ch. XVI).
11. Silver loading (Ch. XVII); Spanish horsemen ambush; officer prisoner; Coombes swims with 3 to recover *Damsel*; Spanish battery at estuary; Jack leads sally; Ralph shot in left leg, struck on head; Skelton carries him; Sir Thomas? (Slingsby not yet).
12. Ch. XIX: Ralph wakes in *Damsel*; father's foot lost; Virginia (planters), Bahamas; *Nonsuch* lost in gale, reunion; *Sol del Esto* taken (~ch. XIX-XX; father wounded; da Silva killed; 300 prisoners). Homeward; Lizard (Ch. XX).
13. 1588 May: Armada news; Portsmouth provisions; Slingsby joins; Plymouth; Catwater; *Pride of Saltash* topmast; Armada passes Fowey? (Howard lets Armada pass); 19-20 July skirmishes; *Revenge*/Drake; Venetian ship at Goodwins; *Damsel* grounded, boarded; Admiral's boats rescue.
14. Fireships (July 28, Calais): Ralph sails *Damsel* as fireship (Howard's order); burns it; sinks between two galleons. Ralph carries letter to Queen; *Distaff*; Queen knights Ralph "Sir Ralph Roy" (Sussex's testimony).
15. Coda: Jack to Pacific; Slingsby at Bramdean; Ralph visited Bordeaux galley; Don Iago captive oarsman, Ralph pleads for lighter treatment.

## Quoted phrases / notable lines
- "'Gainst the might of Spain"; "Obey orders unquestioningly" (Cleat); "Request? Sink me! I never request--I order."
- Invitory text: sale "twenty-nynth daie of June, 1582".
- Queen's words: "Beshrew me!" "Arise, Sir Ralph Roy."
- Howard: "the Channel... one hundred miles over".
- Spelling/transcriber notes: "Grammercy" standardized; "t'gallants" corrected.
